topic: Scopper Gaban's feats on Elbaph, including wounding Nerona Imu and revealing Zoro's Supreme King Haki, prove he really was the Roger Pirates' second strongest member, not their third
title: Scopper Gaban Really Was Roger's Second Strongest Pirate
description:
Even the giants on Elbaph rank Scopper Gaban third strongest of the Roger Pirates, and Gaban furiously corrects them every single time. This is the chapter-cited case for why he's actually right: from clearing a mountain range with two axes to wounding the World Government's secret ruler in single combat, Gaban's resume stacks up directly against Rayleigh's own.

From the Battle of Edd War to the warning he gave Zoro about his own hidden Haki, this traces exactly why Gaban deserves the rank he's spent his whole life fighting for.
comment: Was Scopper Gaban really the Roger Pirates' second strongest member, or does Rayleigh still deserve that spot?

lines.text: Everyone believes Silvers Rayleigh was clearly the Roger Pirates' second strongest member.

shot.search: Rayleigh assumed second strongest Roger crew
shot.fallback: legendary first mate widely assumed to rank highest

lines.text: Chapter 1151 says otherwise: even the New Giant Warrior Pirates rank Scopper Gaban third, and Gaban himself refuses to accept it.

shot.search: Gaban refuses third rank chapter 1151
shot.fallback: furious old warrior correcting an insulting rank

lines.text: So who actually was the Roger Pirates' real second strongest fighter, Rayleigh, or the old man everyone keeps underestimating?

shot.search: Question real second strongest Rayleigh Gaban
shot.fallback: two legendary rivals measured against each other

lines.text: Gaban calls himself the Left Hand of the Pirate King for a reason, and the feats actually back him up.

shot.search: Gaban Left Hand Pirate King feats
shot.fallback: self-given title backed by a lifetime of real feats

lines.text: He fought the World Government's secret ruler directly, and walked away having actually drawn blood from them.

shot.search: Gaban fights Imu draws blood directly
shot.fallback: lone fighter actually wounding the world's hidden ruler

lines.text: Here's the chapter-cited case for why Scopper Gaban deserves the rank he's been fighting for his entire life...

shot.search: Chapter cited case Gaban deserves rank
shot.fallback: overdue recognition decades in the making

lines.text: Scopper Gaban served as the Roger Pirates' navigator, and his fame was said to rival Roger and Rayleigh's own.

shot.search: Gaban navigator fame rivals Roger Rayleigh
shot.fallback: legendary navigator standing among history's most famous pirates

lines.text: Rayleigh is always called the Right Hand of the Pirate King. Gaban is always called the Left Hand.

shot.search: Rayleigh Right Hand Gaban Left Hand titles
shot.fallback: two matching titles describing one captain's closest allies

lines.text: Gaban doesn't care for small talk at all, famously cutting off a conversation about Shyarly's popularity the moment it started.

shot.search: Gaban cuts off small talk Shyarly
shot.fallback: blunt, impatient personality with zero tolerance for idle chat

lines.text: He's quick to get straight to the point too, once suggesting the crew stop a rampaging Kouzuki Oden before real damage was done.

shot.search: Gaban suggests stop Oden rampage quickly
shot.fallback: sharp instincts cutting through chaos before it escalates

lines.text: He was also the first crewmate to voice real frustration with Oden once Oden actually joined the Roger Pirates for good.

shot.search: Gaban first voice frustration Oden joins
shot.fallback: blunt honesty voiced before anyone else dared to say it

lines.text: Gaban understood Roger better than almost anyone on that ship, knowing it was pointless trying to talk his captain out of a fight.

shot.search: Gaban understands Roger pointless talk out
shot.fallback: deep understanding of a captain nobody could ever truly stop

lines.text: He often played the voice of reason against an impulsive, headstrong Roger, who'd just provoke him right back for the effort.

shot.search: Gaban voice reason Roger provokes back
shot.fallback: thankless role played for a captain who never really listened

lines.text: Those two titles were never an accident. They describe two people standing at exactly the same level, just on opposite sides.

shot.search: Titles describe same level opposite sides
shot.fallback: matching titles implying equal standing on either side

lines.text: Gaban is proud of that standing too, correcting anyone who dares call him third strongest instead of second.

shot.search: Gaban proud corrects third strongest claim
shot.fallback: stubborn pride refusing to accept a lesser rank

lines.text: He's also family-oriented in a way that doesn't quite fit the gruff old warrior image fans usually give him.

shot.search: Gaban family oriented not gruff image
shot.fallback: unexpected warmth hiding behind a battle-hardened exterior

lines.text: He considered the Roger Pirates' young apprentices like sons, and genuinely cherishes his own partner Ripley and their son Colon.

shot.search: Gaban cherishes apprentices Ripley son Colon
shot.fallback: gruff warrior revealing a deeply devoted family man

lines.text: He even helped raise Shanks like a son, decades before Shanks ever crossed paths with a young Luffy at all.

shot.search: Gaban raises Shanks like son before Luffy
shot.fallback: legendary bond formed decades before Shanks ever met Luffy

lines.text: Even while critically wounded during a chaotic siege on Elbaph, he still struggled to correct the record on his own rank.

shot.search: Even wounded Gaban corrects record rank
shot.fallback: injured warrior still insisting on the correct ranking

lines.text: Think about that. A man bleeding out mid-battle still cares more about getting his rank right than about the wound itself.

shot.search: Man mid-battle cares rank not wound
shot.fallback: stubborn pride outweighing even a serious injury

lines.text: That's not vanity for its own sake. That's a man who knows exactly what he actually did to earn that rank...

shot.search: Not vanity knows what he earned rank
shot.fallback: earned confidence, not empty pride

lines.text: Early in his career, Gaban single-handedly defeated hundreds of enemy pirates while protecting an injured, recovering Roger.

shot.search: Gaban defeats hundreds protects injured Roger
shot.fallback: lone warrior holding off an entire army for his captain

lines.text: By the time that fight ended, he'd wiped an entire mountain range clean of vegetation with just his two axes.

shot.search: Gaban clears mountain range two axes
shot.fallback: devastating axe strikes leveling an entire mountain range

lines.text: That's exactly how he earned his epithet: Mountain-Eater, a nickname most fans barely even remember today.

shot.search: Mountain-Eater epithet earned forgotten nickname
shot.fallback: legendary title earned through one overwhelming feat

lines.text: His signature technique, Kamudo, infuses his axes with Supreme King Haki and launches bolts of black lightning at the target.

shot.search: Gaban Kamudo axes black lightning Haki
shot.fallback: devastating technique crackling with raw black lightning

lines.text: That technique alone was strong enough to cut clean through the enormous branches of Elbaph's sacred Treasure Tree Adam.

shot.search: Kamudo cuts Treasure Tree Adam branches
shot.fallback: overwhelming strike slicing through a legendary ancient tree

lines.text: Its name is even a clear echo of Roger's own signature move, Kamusari, which says plenty about how closely Gaban studied his captain.

shot.search: Kamudo echoes Roger Kamusari studied captain
shot.fallback: a technique named in quiet tribute to an old captain

lines.text: At the Battle of Edd War, Shiki's entire armada threatened to destroy the Roger Pirates outright if they refused an alliance.

shot.search: Edd War Shiki armada threatens Roger Pirates
shot.fallback: overwhelming fleet threatening to end an entire crew

lines.text: Gaban fought in that battle too, trying to keep a panicking Buggy calm while Roger refused Shiki's offer outright.

shot.search: Gaban calms Buggy Roger refuses Shiki
shot.fallback: steady hand managing a panicking crewmate mid-crisis

lines.text: The Roger Pirates survived that fight only because a storm sank half of Shiki's fleet in the middle of the battle.

shot.search: Storm sinks Shiki fleet Roger Pirates survive
shot.fallback: sudden storm turning the tide of an impossible battle

lines.text: Gaban also kept in touch with Crocus and Shanks for decades after the crew disbanded, respected by both to this day.

shot.search: Gaban respected Crocus Shanks decades later
shot.fallback: lasting respect carried across decades by old crewmates

lines.text: At the treasure hunt on God Valley, Gaban nearly lost his axes outright to Captain John's magnet powers while gathering loot.

shot.search: Gaban nearly loses axes John magnet God Valley
shot.fallback: dangerous magnetic pull threatening a trusted weapon

lines.text: He tried to warn Roger about it, but Roger pushed forward anyway, trusting his crew to handle whatever came next.

shot.search: Gaban warns Roger pushes forward trusts crew
shot.fallback: urgent warning brushed aside by a fearless captain

lines.text: Gaban and Rayleigh rushed inland together to help pull both Roger and Garp out of the collapsing island afterward.

shot.search: Gaban Rayleigh rush pull Roger Garp out
shot.fallback: two trusted lieutenants racing to save their captain

lines.text: Years after Roger's death, Gaban settled on Elbaph and became close with the giants there, known locally simply as Ya-san.

shot.search: Gaban settles Elbaph known Ya-san locally
shot.fallback: legendary warrior living quietly among an entire island's giants

lines.text: He helped try to save the children of the Walrus School when they were taken hostage, only failing when his own son was threatened.

shot.search: Gaban tries save Walrus School children hostage
shot.fallback: desperate rescue attempt halted by a threat to his own family

lines.text: Even in retirement, surrounded by people who respected him purely for his strength, Gaban never once stopped being the fighter Roger relied on.

shot.search: Gaban retirement never stops fighter Roger relied
shot.fallback: retired legend who never truly put the fight down

lines.text: Road, one of Elbaph's own giants, still knew him instantly as Ya-san, a reputation built on decades of quiet, local trust.

shot.search: Road recognizes Gaban Ya-san local trust
shot.fallback: quiet local legend recognized instantly by a young giant

lines.text: He even introduced himself to Luffy's crew as the self-declared preacher of love, which somehow fits a man this contradictory perfectly.

shot.search: Gaban preacher of love introduces himself
shot.fallback: self-given title that oddly fits a man full of contradictions

lines.text: None of that reads like a third-strongest résumé. It reads like someone who was there for every major fight Roger ever had...

shot.search: Not third strongest résumé every major fight
shot.fallback: a résumé that reads far higher than third place

lines.text: Decades later, on Elbaph, Gaban senses a strange, overwhelming Haki before almost anyone else on the entire island does.

shot.search: Gaban senses strange Haki Elbaph first
shot.fallback: sharp instincts catching a threat before anyone else

lines.text: He eventually confronts Nerona Imu directly, the secret ruler of the entire World Government, in single combat.

shot.search: Gaban confronts Imu single combat directly
shot.fallback: lone warrior standing against the world's secret ruler

lines.text: Imu personally admits it was a mistake ever letting the Roger Pirates survive God Valley, specifically because of threats like Gaban.

shot.search: Imu admits mistake letting Roger survive
shot.fallback: world ruler openly regretting an old, costly decision

lines.text: That's not a throwaway compliment. That's the single most powerful being in the story calling Gaban a genuine mistake to leave alive.

shot.search: Powerful being calls Gaban genuine mistake
shot.fallback: the highest possible compliment from the worst possible source

lines.text: The fight costs Gaban his entire left arm, but he still manages to actually wound Imu in the exchange.

shot.search: Fight costs Gaban arm wounds Imu
shot.fallback: devastating trade costing an arm but landing a real hit

lines.text: He does all of this specifically to buy time and save Luffy, already knowing exactly how steep that price would be.

shot.search: Gaban saves Luffy knowing steep price
shot.fallback: knowing sacrifice made without a moment of real hesitation

lines.text: Before the clash, Gaban had already lost faith that Luffy was taking the title of Pirate King seriously enough to deserve it.

shot.search: Gaban lost faith Luffy deserve title before
shot.fallback: wavering faith placed on hold before a decisive moment

lines.text: He still fights for him anyway, telling Imu directly that his old crew is still waiting for Luffy to prove them right.

shot.search: Gaban fights anyway tells Imu crew waiting
shot.fallback: conditional faith still acted on despite private doubt

lines.text: That's not blind loyalty. That's a calculated bet made by someone who's already watched one Pirate King earn the title from scratch.

shot.search: Not blind loyalty calculated bet experienced
shot.fallback: an experienced gambler's bet, not a naive act of faith

lines.text: Urging Luffy to leave Elbaph afterward, Gaban makes sure the bet actually survives the day, whatever happens to himself.

shot.search: Gaban urges Luffy leave bet survives
shot.fallback: selfless priority placed above his own immediate survival

lines.text: Rayleigh's own biggest confirmed feats come from decades earlier, mostly against ordinary Marines and pirates, not against a god.

shot.search: Rayleigh feats decades earlier ordinary Marines
shot.fallback: older feats measured against far smaller stakes

lines.text: Even Observation Haki tells the same story. Gaban can sense Haki from a great distance and use its rare Future Vision form too.

shot.search: Gaban Observation Haki distance Future Vision
shot.fallback: razor-sharp senses detecting threats from miles away

lines.text: That advanced Future Vision once showed him his own son Colon's end before it even happened, a vision he couldn't act on in time.

shot.search: Future Vision shows Colon fate too late
shot.fallback: painful glimpse of the future arriving just too late

lines.text: Only a tiny handful of people in the entire story have ever shown that specific, advanced level of Observation Haki.

shot.search: Tiny handful advanced Observation Haki level
shot.fallback: an elite ability shared by only a handful of fighters

lines.text: Gaban's resume now includes drawing blood from the actual ruler of the entire world. That's not a small gap to ignore...

shot.search: Gaban resume includes wounding world ruler
shot.fallback: staggering feat that changes the entire conversation

lines.text: Here's the direct comparison fans keep avoiding: Rayleigh fought Kizaru to a draw decades after the crew disbanded, Haki negated.

shot.search: Rayleigh draws Kizaru decades after disbanded
shot.fallback: aging legend still matching a modern Admiral

lines.text: Gaban fought and wounded the actual ruler of the World Government, decades after the exact same disbandment.

shot.search: Gaban wounds World Government ruler same era
shot.fallback: equally aging legend landing a hit on the world's secret ruler

lines.text: Both of them are still operating at a monstrous level deep into old age. That part genuinely isn't in question.

shot.search: Both monstrous level old age not question
shot.fallback: two legends still performing at an impossible level

lines.text: The only real question is which fight actually says more about where someone ranks: a draw against an Admiral, or a wound on a god.

shot.search: Question which fight says more ranking
shot.fallback: two legendary feats weighed directly against each other

lines.text: Hajrudin and the other giants call Gaban third strongest anyway, based on old rumors instead of anything he's actually done lately.

shot.search: Giants call Gaban third based rumors
shot.fallback: outdated reputation ignoring decades of real, recent evidence

lines.text: That reputation likely comes from a simpler, older era, when Rayleigh's constant presence at Roger's side was simply easier to track.

shot.search: Reputation older era Rayleigh easier track
shot.fallback: an outdated rumor rooted in an older, simpler era

lines.text: Gaban, by contrast, wandered as a navigator, leaving fewer easy stories behind for the rest of the world to actually remember.

shot.search: Gaban wandered navigator fewer stories remembered
shot.fallback: a quieter legacy earned through distance instead of spectacle

lines.text: Gaban's own fury at that ranking isn't an old man being touchy. It's someone correcting a reputation stuck decades in the past.

shot.search: Gaban fury correcting outdated reputation
shot.fallback: justified frustration at an outdated, lazy reputation

lines.text: Update the résumé with what he actually did on Elbaph, and third strongest simply doesn't hold up anymore...

shot.search: Updated résumé third strongest does not hold
shot.fallback: an outdated ranking collapsing under new evidence

lines.text: Gaban's bond with Shanks runs deeper than most fans realize, going all the way back to the day the crew found him as a baby.

shot.search: Gaban bond Shanks baby found crew
shot.fallback: legendary bond beginning the day a baby was found

lines.text: He physically consoled Shanks when Shanks felt ashamed about the circumstances of his own birth, telling him everyone has a purpose.

shot.search: Gaban consoles Shanks ashamed birth purpose
shot.fallback: gentle reassurance offered to a deeply ashamed young man

lines.text: Decades later, Shanks still visits Gaban on Elbaph just to drink and reminisce about everything that's changed since Roger died.

shot.search: Shanks visits Gaban Elbaph reminisce decades
shot.fallback: lasting friendship revisited over quiet drinks decades later

lines.text: When Garp told Gaban that Roger had fathered a son, Gaban was the one who warned Shanks that bloodline alone guarantees nothing.

shot.search: Gaban warns Shanks bloodline guarantees nothing
shot.fallback: blunt wisdom tempering a young man's high expectations

lines.text: That's the same blunt honesty he'd later give Zoro: respect the bloodline or the title, but earn the actual power yourself.

shot.search: Same blunt honesty Zoro earn power
shot.fallback: consistent philosophy applied across two different generations

lines.text: Gaban even recognized Luffy's carefree attitude toward danger as the exact same trait that defined his old captain Roger.

shot.search: Gaban recognizes Luffy carefree trait Roger
shot.fallback: familiar recklessness echoing across an entire generation

lines.text: He openly told Luffy he wouldn't be worthy of the title Pirate King unless he took his own dream seriously enough.

shot.search: Gaban tells Luffy worthy dream seriously
shot.fallback: blunt challenge testing whether a dream is truly earned

lines.text: He also teased Luffy about Shanks loaning him the straw hat rather than just giving it to him outright, baiting him into a fight.

shot.search: Gaban teases Luffy straw hat loan fight
shot.fallback: playful taunt deliberately provoking a famously hot-headed pirate

lines.text: That's Gaban's actual teaching style: provoke first, test the reaction, and only then decide if someone's actually worth his time.

shot.search: Gaban teaching style provoke test worth
shot.fallback: unconventional method testing character before offering real respect

lines.text: Zoro and Luffy both lost their tempers at him, right up until he casually equipped his axes and showed them why that was a mistake...

shot.search: Zoro Luffy lose temper Gaban axes mistake
shot.fallback: overconfident challengers quickly reminded of who they're actually facing

lines.text: Before Gaban ever clashes with Imu, he stops to warn Zoro about something Zoro didn't even know about himself.

shot.search: Gaban warns Zoro something unknown himself
shot.fallback: sharp mentor noticing a hidden power nobody else caught

lines.text: He senses that Zoro carries Supreme King Haki, a power so rare most users never even realize they have it.

shot.search: Gaban senses Zoro Supreme King Haki rare
shot.fallback: rare power quietly confirmed by a sharp old observer

lines.text: Gaban is appalled that Zoro never noticed this himself, criticizing him directly for not taking his own power seriously enough.

shot.search: Gaban appalled Zoro never noticed criticizes
shot.fallback: blunt criticism aimed at an unaware young swordsman

lines.text: He reminds Zoro bluntly that as Luffy's second, he should always be ready to back up his captain in a real fight.

shot.search: Gaban reminds Zoro second back captain
shot.fallback: pointed reminder about a second's actual responsibility

lines.text: Gaban acknowledges Haki as a power that has to be understood and tamed, not just stumbled into by accident.

shot.search: Gaban acknowledges Haki understood tamed
shot.fallback: disciplined philosophy treating raw power as a craft, not luck

lines.text: He criticizes Zoro specifically because someone serving under an Emperor of the Sea should already be meticulous about his own strength.

shot.search: Gaban criticizes Zoro meticulous own strength
shot.fallback: high standard expected of anyone serving a true Emperor

lines.text: That single standard, demanding real mastery instead of raw talent alone, is the exact same standard Gaban held himself to for decades.

shot.search: Same standard mastery Gaban held himself
shot.fallback: a lifelong personal standard now passed to someone new

lines.text: That's not a passing comment from a random old giant-island local. That's a verified second strongest pirate passing down real knowledge.

shot.search: Not passing comment verified pirate knowledge
shot.fallback: hard-earned wisdom passed from one legend to a rising one

lines.text: Only someone who has actually lived at that level could spot a power like that in someone else so quickly.

shot.search: Only someone lived that level spots power
shot.fallback: rare insight only available at the very top of the ladder

lines.text: Rayleigh trained Luffy directly for two years. Gaban, in a single conversation, gave Zoro something just as valuable.

shot.search: Rayleigh trains Luffy Gaban gives Zoro value
shot.fallback: two very different lessons, equally valuable in the end

lines.text: One lesson took two years of patient training. The other took one sharp sentence from a man who'd already lived through everything Zoro was about to face.

shot.search: One lesson years other one sentence
shot.fallback: two radically different paces reaching the exact same destination

lines.text: That's the real value of having someone who was actually there decades ago still standing on the front lines today...

shot.search: Value having someone there decades still standing
shot.fallback: a living bridge between two completely different eras

lines.text: So here's the actual verdict: Scopper Gaban really was the Roger Pirates' second strongest member, not their third.

shot.search: Verdict Gaban second strongest not third
shot.fallback: final ranking settled by the weight of real evidence

lines.text: Some fans will say rank doesn't even matter this late in the story, that it's just an old man's pride talking.

shot.search: Fans say rank does not matter pride
shot.fallback: fair dismissal questioning why any of this matters

lines.text: That's a fair point to raise. In the middle of a war against Imu, rank really shouldn't be the priority.

shot.search: Fair point middle war rank not priority
shot.fallback: valid criticism the theory does not fully dismiss

lines.text: But Gaban correcting his rank mid-battle isn't about ego. It's the one thing he has left to prove after losing an arm for Luffy.

shot.search: Gaban correcting rank not ego proof
shot.fallback: small correction carrying far more weight than it first seems

lines.text: Rayleigh got two years to train the next generation in peace. Gaban got one single fight to prove everything at once.

shot.search: Rayleigh two years Gaban one fight prove
shot.fallback: two legends given very different windows to prove themselves

lines.text: He used that one fight to wound a god, warn a swordsman, and save a future Pirate King, all at the same time.

shot.search: Gaban one fight wounds warns saves
shot.fallback: a single fight accomplishing three separate legendary feats

lines.text: Add in decades of raising Shanks, warning him about the weight of his own bloodline, and the picture only gets bigger.

shot.search: Add decades raising Shanks warning bloodline
shot.fallback: an already overwhelming resume growing even larger

lines.text: A third-strongest pirate doesn't end up shaping that many of the story's most important people across that many decades.

shot.search: Third strongest does not shape many decades
shot.fallback: an unlikely spread of influence for a supposedly lesser rank

lines.text: That's not a third-strongest performance by any reasonable measure. That's a man finally proving what the rumors always undersold.

shot.search: Not third strongest proving rumors undersold
shot.fallback: overdue proof finally catching up to an undersold reputation

lines.text: It's also worth saying plainly: none of this is a knock against Rayleigh, whose own legend never actually needed defending in the first place.

shot.search: Not knock against Rayleigh legend defended
shot.fallback: fair acknowledgment that both legends can stand at the top

lines.text: Two people can stand at the very top of the exact same crew without either one needing to be pushed down to get there.

shot.search: Two people top same crew no pushing down
shot.fallback: room at the top for two legends, not just one

lines.text: Gaban spent his whole life being called the wrong number. Elbaph is where the number finally caught up to the man.

shot.search: Gaban wrong number Elbaph catches up
shot.fallback: a lifelong argument finally settled by one decisive day

lines.text: He lost an arm proving it, which is exactly the kind of price a second strongest pays and a third strongest never has to.

shot.search: Lost arm price second strongest pays
shot.fallback: a genuine cost that only the truly second-strongest would pay
